content.body:
The PaK 35/36 was the standard German AT gun at the start of the war, having seen successful service in Spain. By the invasion of France however, it was unable to penetrate the armor on a number of Allied heavy tanks.
Because of this inadequacy, soldiers dubbed it the "door knocker." Apparently all it did was knock on the outside of enemy vehicles to let them know you were there. It was, however, quite accurate and very mobile, but by 1940 this 37 mm AT gun simply did not have enough power to be truly effective.
AT gunners will find that this gun is a pleasure to shoot, as long as you are not shooting at tanks that you can't kill. It is exceptionally accurate with a flat shot and has very little dispersion. When ammunition isn't an issue some players have found it serves well as a 1,500+ m sniper rifle. If you are shooting at enemy tanks, take advantage of this precision to try to compensate for the poor penetration and by aiming at vision blocks, turret rings, guns, and tracks. Firing at tanks in general, make sure you have a good shot on a vulnerable spot or on the rear/side aspect.
Being relatively fast to limber/unlimber, or "deploy," it is nimble on the field. Take advantage of this by relocating frequently.
CREW POSITIONS: 1 Commander 2 Gunner
